transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Eric Tan (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Lattice Head of ML), Jon Rivera (Lattice Infrastructure Lead), Priya Shah (Lattice FinOps)

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery to understand Lattice AI's expected token volumes, latency SLOs, and budget constraints; evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options; identify next steps for pricing and a technical benchmark.

Transcript:
00:00 Sofia Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we know you're on a tight timeline so we'll run through cost and deployment options. can folks hear me okay?
00:05 Maya Patel: yeah hearing you, thanks Sofia.
00:08 Eric Tan: hey all, quick intro - i'm Eric on the SE side, i'll jump into batching and runtime questions.
00:12 Maya Patel: awesome. quick context from us - Lattice runs an assistant embedded in product and a heavy batch embedding pipeline for search. we're looking at roughly 10 million tokens a month for the assistant, plus about 2 million embeddings. cost is the big unknown.
00:30 Priya Shah: and from finops perspective we have a hard cap for proof of concept of $6k/month, but we can scale if unit economics make sense.
00:40 Jon Rivera: infra constraints - we prefer VPC integrations, and some workloads must stay in our private network because of data residency. we do have capacity to host but want to understand ops overhead.
00:52 Sofia Martinez: great, that gives us a good baseline. high level: Redwood offers Hosted (quick to start), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput), and Private (VPC or on-prem). each has different pricing/levers.
01:05 Maya Patel: can you give ballpark per-token numbers and how batching or caching affects them? that's the core.
01:12 Eric Tan: sure - quick caveat: numbers vary by model family and quantization. but ballpark hosted inference for open LLMs is in the order of $0.00002 to $0.0002 per token depending on model size and sequence length. dedicated reserved capacity shifts to a cost-per-instance model which often maps to lower per-token at scale because of amortized GPU time.
01:33 Priya Shah: so on hosted, is the per-token price fixed? or do we get volume tiers?
01:38 Sofia Martinez: hosted has tiered pricing - volume discounts kick in and we also expose batching, prefix caching, and KV cache settings that reduce effective token counts. for example, if you have a lot of repeated prefixes, prefix caching can cut generated tokens by 20-40% on typical chat workloads.
01:58 Eric Tan: also continuous batching - our runtime groups requests to improve GPU utilization. if your typical prompt+response length is small, batching increases throughput and reduces per-token cost, but it does add a small additional latency delta. we can tune batch windows to hit p99 SLOs.
02:18 Jon Rivera: what about Dedicated - what's the pricing model and commit?
02:21 Sofia Martinez: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools. pricing is a monthly commit for capacity; customers pick capacity tiers. it gives you predictable throughput and lower unit costs at steady state. you still pay for reserved capacity but we offer burst options for traffic spikes.
02:37 Maya Patel: any numbers on the unit drop? like, if we go Dedicated for our 10M tokens, how much would we save?
02:42 Eric Tan: rough calc - if hosted is ~ $0.00008 per token on average for the model you referenced, 10M tokens is $800; but that seems low because embeddings cost separately. embeddings are priced differently - say $0.002 per embedding for that model family - 2M embeddings would be $4,000. together that's $4.8k/month hosted rough. with Dedicated and smarter batching/caching we might reduce the embedding cost a bit via optimized batch pipelines and quantization, perhaps down 15-25% overall. but exact savings depend on how embedding generation can be batched on GPU - sometimes embedding workloads are cheaper to run on CPU or dedicated smaller GPUs which changes the math.
03:26 Priya Shah: those hosted numbers get us close to the $6k POC cap, good sign. for Dedicated, is there an upfront or minimum?
03:33 Sofia Martinez: typically a monthly minimum for Dedicated but we have flexible pilots. we can structure a 3-month pilot with a reduced commit to prove out throughput and measure unit economics.
03:42 Jon Rivera: about Private VPC/on-prem - we want data never to leave our VPC for some endpoints. how does that change cost?
03:49 Eric Tan: Private is more of a licensing + support + infra cost - you pay for the software and support, plus you host infrastructure. If you already have GPUs, it can be cheaper at scale but you take on ops costs. for strict data residency the Private option removes egress concerns but the total TCO includes provisioning, maintenance, and possible model optimization work.
04:12 Maya Patel: what about quantization - can we use int8 or 4-bit to reduce GPU memory and cost? any effect on quality?
04:19 Eric Tan: yes, quantization profiles are a big lever. we support 4-bit INT4/INT8 workflows and model recompilation to preserve accuracy. often you get 2x-3x throughput improvements for generative workloads at modest quality loss; for embeddings we test to ensure vectors stay within your similarity thresholds. we'll run evals on your validation prompts to quantify quality delta.
04:45 Priya Shah: curious about caching - you mentioned KV cache and prefix cache. can you explain cost impact in plain terms?
04:50 Sofia Martinez: prefix caching stores common prompt prefixes so you don't re-tokenize or re-execute early transformer layers; KV cache saves key/value activations for long-running sessions so continued turns are cheaper. in billing terms, effective billed tokens go down because we only bill for the delta in some setups or we reduce GPU compute per token, which reduces price. it's workload dependent though.
05:15 Jon Rivera: does Redwood bill per-hosted token regardless of caching?
05:20 Sofia Martinez: on Hosted, we bill per token but provide configuration and recommendations that lower consumed tokens and compute. for Dedicated/Private we model cost as reserved capacity, so billing is different - it's a capacity fee plus marginal compute for bursts.
05:34 Maya Patel: we have a use case where assistant sessions average 7 turns, and 60% of turns repeat the same system prompt. sounds like prefix caching would help a lot.
05:44 Eric Tan: yeah that's a great fit. we typically see 25-40% reduction in compute for that pattern. we'll need a sample of actual prompts to run a simulation.
05:56 Priya Shah: for POC we need a clear cost estimate line-itemized - embeddings, generation, storage, any retention costs, plus potential infra fees. can you provide that?
06:05 Sofia Martinez: absolutely - we'll produce a bill estimate using your numbers; Eric will run batch sims and give recommended batch sizes and expected per-token effective cost.
06:15 Jon Rivera: one more - latency SLOs. we target 300ms p95 for assistant responses. can Redwood meet that on hosted?
06:24 Eric Tan: depends on model and region. for smaller open models and with tuned batching you can hit 300ms p95 for short responses. for larger models or long outputs it's harder. Dedicated reduces tail latency variability since you control capacity and avoid noisy neighbors.
06:40 Maya Patel: we also need SOC2 compliance and SSO for our enterprise users. is Redwood SOC2?
06:46 Sofia Martinez: yes, we are SOC 2 Type II - we'll share the security whitepaper and audit artifacts. we also support SAML SSO and RBAC.
06:56 Priya Shah: encryption/KMS - can you integrate with our KMS?
07:00 Eric Tan: yes, for Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; Hosted supports encryption at rest and customer-managed keys for higher tiers.
07:10 Maya Patel: what does the benchmark look like? we want to run a throughput test for embeddings and a p99 latency test for chat.
07:17 Eric Tan: recommended: 2-hour benchmark - first hour embeddings batch throughput at your typical batch sizes, second hour chat with synthetic traffic reflecting your session patterns. we'll run with and without prefix/KV caching and test quantized models.
07:32 Jon Rivera: will you need access to our VPC for the benchmark?
07:35 Eric Tan: for Private it's straightforward, for Hosted we run tests from our infra but can simulate your traffic. if you want end-to-end latency from your network, we'll need a peering or a test harness inside your VPC.
07:48 Priya Shah: default billing cadence for hosted is monthly invoiced?
07:51 Sofia Martinez: yes monthly; Dedicated is monthly commit, Private typically has a contract with invoicing terms.
07:59 Maya Patel: any hidden fees - egress, logs, observability?
08:03 Sofia Martinez: observability is included at baseline; we have retention tiers for logs/metrics that can be an add-on. egress is standard cloud egress, but we can discuss regional pricing.
08:15 Jon Rivera: on the topic of ops - if we go Dedicated or Private, how much day-to-day maintenance do you take on?
08:22 Sofia Martinez: for Dedicated, Redwood manages the serving runtime, autoscaling policies, and rollout features; you get managed upgrades. For Private we offer a managed service layer or a self-hosted option; we can tailor the support level.
08:36 Maya Patel: ok practical next steps?
08:39 Sofia Martinez: recap: 1) we'll send a hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet and a POC proposal scoped to 10M tokens + 2M embeddings; 2) Eric will run cost sims and batching recommendations; 3) security pack (SOC2, SAML docs) will be shared; 4) schedule 2-hour benchmark - Lattice to pick time windows.
08:57 Priya Shah: timeline - we want decision on POC budget in 2 weeks. can you turn around the pricing fast?
09:02 Sofia Martinez: yes, we'll aim to send pricing by tomorrow EOD and have Eric's sim within 48 hours.
09:08 Maya Patel: sounds good. any other questions from your side?
09:11 Jon Rivera: one - competitor comparison; how are you different from OpenCloud AI?
09:15 Sofia Martinez: Redwood focuses on production economics and uniform tooling across hosted, dedicated, private. we provide explicit levers (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles) and observability to tie quality regressions back to prompts, which is a gap we hear from customers of OpenCloud AI.
09:31 Maya Patel: perfect. we'll share prompt samples and embedding workloads after the call.
09:35 Sofia Martinez: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and I'll cc Priya on cost breakdown.
09:40 End of call.
